purpose: Stop partial and weak evidence being graded Strong: give the security judge a per-turn marking scheme and require it to copy the facts it grades on. Compare with the judge without a marking scheme on the same screenshot readings.
code_version: d13567ec (marking scheme, three levels, anchored actions); recorded before the separate bf16/memory check
method: Identity-management scenario, saved incident timeline. Turn 1: the saved turn's three screenshots, judged with the coach-written best action ('Detect IAM Activity') and with the repaired best action ('Check GuardDuty Finding'). Turns 2-5: evidence rebuilt from the timeline with the current code, rendered, read once by the VLM (readings cached and reused for every judge run), judged with the code-written anchor action. Same one-sentence typed justification for every case. Expected verdict = the evidence's authored support role.
limitations: One scenario (identity-management) and one incident timeline.
Turns 2-5 use the code-written anchor action, not coach-written actions.
The VLM and judge only; coach feedback and progress changes were not exercised.
Raw VLM outputs and full judge replies were kept in a temporary folder that was later cleared; the verdict tables below were copied from the run logs printed during the session.
